item.title: CT, NY senators say they won’t vote to fund ICE after MN shooting ahead of government shutdown deadline
item.description: Ten Democratic senators have to vote with Republicans for a set of funding bills that include an increased budget for ICE before the Friday deadline or the government shuts down. Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) said his caucus won’t vote to increase funding for ICE.

item.title: Hartford Democrat Doug McCrory denies wrongdoing
item.description: State Senator Doug McCrory (D-Hartford) has denied any wrongdoing after an audit released last week suggested potential fraud and misappropriation of funds at a Hartford nonprofit, where he helped direct more than $15 million in state funds over the past five years.

item.title: Snowstorm, icy roads grip CT and Long Island
item.description: Heavy snow and icy conditions covered much of Connecticut and Long Island, dumping more than a foot in many areas, disrupting travel and prompting government closures and highway restrictions.

item.title: Tong demands Grok remove nonconsensual AI sexual content
item.description: Connecticut Attorney General William Tong has joined a coalition demanding that the platform X stop its AI chatbot from creating nonconsensual sexual images.

item.title: CT Senate Democrats seek to allow civil rights lawsuits against federal officers
item.description: Connecticut Senate Democrats want to expand that state’s civil rights law in response to the killing of Alex Pretti in Minneapolis by federal officers on Saturday.

item.title: New federal guidance targets healthier eating habits
item.description: With a new year well underway, many people are settling into, or maybe giving up on, health and wellness goals. At the same time, the Trump administration has rolled out an updated food pyramid meant to guide Americans’ eating habits.

item.title: What actually happened on July 4, 1776?
item.description: The big day is July 4, 2026. It’ll mark a quarter millennium since the final text of the Declaration of Independence was approved by the Second Continental Congress. It severed political ties between the 13 colonies and Great Britain.

item.title: Blumenthal to join fellow Senate Democrats in voting 'no' on DHS funding
item.description: U.S. Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) has said he’ll join fellow Senate Democrats this week in voting no on funding for ICE and the Department of Homeland Security.

item.title: CT service plaza workers begin bargaining after historic unionization
item.description: Workers at Connecticut’s 23 Service Plazas on I-95, I-395, and Route 15 have started bargaining with their employer, Applegreen, for better pay. They unionized months ago.

item.title: Contemporary art at The Aldrich
item.description: The Aldrich in Ridgefield, Connecticut, is unusual for a museum. It doesn’t have any permanent collections, and it features only contemporary artists and their work. WSHU’s Randye Kaye takes listeners on a guided tour through the museum’s galleries to discover what’s new in contemporary art.
